name: Madrid Deep Space Communications Complex
description: The Spanish station of NASA's Deep Space Network, operated by INTA under a Spain-US agreement. It has one 70 m antenna (DSS-63) and five 34 m antennas.
highlights: It has supported Mariner 4, Apollo, Voyager 1 and 2, Cassini-Huygens, Rosetta, New Horizons and the James Webb Space Telescope.
On 20 April 2024 all six of its antennas were arrayed to receive Voyager 1 data, the first time six DSN antennas were arrayed at once.
